swap_risks: CRITICAL OP-AMP VS COMPARATOR TRAP: OPA333AIDBVR is a opamp with push-pull output while TLV3201AIDBVR is a comparator with push-pull output. Even with identical pinouts, an open-collector comparator CANNOT pull high without an external pull-up resistor and lacks internal Miller compensation — dropping it into a linear negative-feedback op-amp circuit causes severe oscillation; conversely, using an op-amp as a comparator causes slow overdrive recovery and output saturation lag.

CAUTION PRECISION OFFSET SHIFT: Maximum Vos differs by 300x (OPA333AIDBVR: 0.01 mV p.7 vs TLV3201AIDBVR: 3 mV p.5); high-gain DC sensor stages may lose accuracy or require zero-drift chopper filtering.
engineering_verdict: OPA333AIDBVR (Texas Instruments, SOT-23-5) and TLV3201AIDBVR (Texas Instruments, SOT-23-5) are Level 2 Functional / Tuning Required replacements: while the footprint is physically compatible, engineering review and passive/circuit adjustments are mandatory due to device kind / output stage mismatch (opamp/push-pull vs comparator/push-pull); input offset voltage Vos differs >= 10x. Key datasheet deltas: device type is opamp (push-pull) vs comparator (push-pull), supply limit is 5.5 V (p.5) vs 5.5 V (p.4), max Vos is 0.01 mV (p.7) vs 3 mV (p.5), input bias current is 70 pA (p.7) vs 1 pA (p.5), and Iq/ch is 17 µA (p.7) vs 40 µA (p.5). Always validate pinout orientation (TOP_VIEW p.3 vs TOP_VIEW p.3), thermal margin (θJA 220.8 vs 237.8 °C/W), and official manufacturer datasheets on hardware prototypes before production release.
